en.headline: Burmese python spotted near Jardine Noonday Gun in Causeway Bay
en.dek: A two-to-three-metre snake was filmed on Victoria Park Road on Sunday night; an expert linked the appearance to recent heavy rain flooding natural habitats.
body: A Burmese python measuring roughly two to three metres was filmed slithering across a pavement near the Jardine Noonday Gun in Causeway Bay on Sunday evening, prompting widespread discussion on social media.

A jogger recorded the reptile at around 11pm along Victoria Park Road. Kadoorie Farm and Botanic Garden identified it as a Burmese python from its geometric patterns and colouration. The non-venomous species is the only snake protected under Hong Kong’s Wild Animals Protection Ordinance.

Victor Wong Long-yin of Cheung Chau Animal Care said recent heavy rain could have flooded the snake’s natural habitat and driven it into urban areas. The social media clip had attracted thousands of views and comments by Monday evening.

zh.headline: 銅鑼灣近午炮台現緬甸蟒 專家指或與大雨有關
zh.dek: 周日晚有人在維園道近怡和午炮台拍攝到一條長約兩至三米的蟒蛇，專家指近日大雨可能迫使其離開自然生境。
body: 周日晚約11時，一名慢跑者在銅鑼灣維園道近怡和午炮台拍攝到一條長約兩至三米的蛇隻在行人路爬行，片段在社交媒體廣泛流傳。
嘉道理農場暨植物園根據其幾何花紋及顏色，確認為緬甸蟒。該物種無毒，是本港《野生動物保護條例》下唯一受保護的蛇類。
長洲動物關注組教育部主管黃朗然表示，近日大雨可能令蟒蛇的自然生境水浸，迫使其進入市區。相關片段至周一晚已累積數千個讚好及留言。
